card.title: The Natchez Indians — Natchez National Historical Park
card.annotation: Brief park history explicitly connects Natchez ancestors and communities with southwest Mississippi. Used for historical geography only. Its sweeping departure and near-annihilation language is not adopted as an account of continuing Natchez identities or rights.
card.contentReviewScope: Complete short article read; map citation uses opening geography and historical mound-center paragraphs. Updated August16,2024.

proposedSection.title: A historical Mississippi connection
proposedSection.text: Natchez historical communities are explicitly connected with southwest Mississippi in the park's account. This is a regional reading route, rather than a limit on the geography or identity of later descendant communities.

card.title: Mingo

card.annotation: Short specialist account explains changing outside uses of Mingo and mixed Ohio Valley communities. It is not evidence for a single Mingo language, government or exclusive homeland.
card.contentReviewScope: Complete short article read, especially naming and West Virginia conflict paragraphs. Last revised April25,2024.

proposedSection.title: A historical name and regional activity

nativeHawaiian.result: No material identity or source-scope misstatement found in the proposed guide.
checked: The guide distinguishes Native Hawaiian identity from all state residents, a particular program definition and any single institution.
Its scope note correctly keeps Hawaiʻi a Pacific archipelago rather than recategorizing it as continental North America.

The1993 resolution text was independently opened: operative apology at107 Stat1513, instrument-specific definition in section2 on1513, non-settlement disclaimer in section3 on1514, approval November23,1993. These match the draft.

OHA is described as a state agency rather than a sovereign government; place-specific education/stewardship accounts are attributed. Four substantive collections plus one supporting item are candidly labeled source-guide.
nativeHawaiian.limits: The three community-organization pages and UH naming item were evaluated against the saved inspection scope/proposed text, not independently re-fetched in this limited pass. No exhaustive legal/history review is claimed.

westVirginia.result: No material claim-scope misstatement found in the geographic draft.
checked: Independent full e-WV Mingo read confirms explicit West Virginia conflict connection and Pennsylvania/Ohio home-village distinction; the draft preserves that difference.
Shawnee routes are stated as historical activity and influence, not exclusive territory or current government location.
Susquehannock displacement is expressly tentative and community-attributed; the draft does not turn that source into a verified legal or continuous-settlement conclusion.
The unrelated Mingo/Kewa legacy card is a genuine fix and is included with its exact object above.
westVirginia.limits: The Shawnee and Susquehannock underlying passages were not freshly re-opened in this pass; their drafted source attribution, inspection notes and uncertainty were checked.

greenland.result: No material identity/geography misstatement found in the proposed replacement route.
checked: Independent direct read of Visit Greenland section5 confirms Kalaallit/Greenlandic Inuit geographic wording, and its footer identifies Government of Greenland ownership.
The draft does not copy the page's dated percentages, conflate every resident with Kalaallit, or infer separate regional identities.
ICC is kept a circumpolar organization, not the government of Greenlandic communities.
greenland.limits: The tourism source is a narrow popular geography introduction with broad terminology; it should remain supporting rather than authoritative for all regional self-designations. ICC's source text was not independently re-opened in this pass.

integrationNotes: Deduplicate proposed supporting cards against any map-support cards root has already added by URL. IDs here are suggestions; do not duplicate an existing exact work.
Any removed sourceId must also be removed/replaced in section sourceIds arrays. Rebuild should catch dangling citations.
All replacement cards are countsTowardMinimum:false; this bounded map/editorial pass is not a twelve-source deep-profile phase.
Keep every owner-supplied URL in the separate lead ledger if applicable. Removing a wrong source card does not require erasing its provenance.
The earlier Natchez 'unrelated' characterization is explicitly corrected above. Useful Natchitoches place-page history is retained rather than discarded based on its title.

Six removal candidates are scoped to source fit: three unequivocal document/people mismatches, one unrelated people card already raised in the WV draft, and two visitor/county pages wrongly supplying identity citations. No other canonical sources were edited.
